sections.heading: Sri Rajiv Gandhi College of Dental Sciences vs The Oxford Dental College for BDS: which is better in 2026
paragraphs: This page cannot name a placement winner, because neither college has a BDS placement record in our database.

The Oxford Dental College has the only recorded year-wise total here, at ₹2.40 lakh. Sri Rajiv Gandhi College of Dental Sciences has no fee row on this page, so you must get its official circular before you budget.

sections.heading: Fees: what our records show
paragraphs: Sri Rajiv Gandhi College of Dental Sciences has no BDS fee row on this page. Do not guess the fee. Ask the college for its current official notice, including any state-quota figure.
The Oxford Dental College has a recorded year-wise total of ₹2.40 lakh. Treat this as a recorded year fee, not a confirmed five-year total, until you check the official circular.

sections.heading: Placements compared
paragraphs: Neither side has a placement row on this page. Do not assume a package that we do not hold.
Ask each college for its latest official internship or placement report, and compare the same graduating year.

sections.heading: Admission and eligibility
paragraphs: Both sides list NEET on this page. BDS admission is through NEET-UG and the relevant state or All India counselling.
Read the current official counselling notices for eligibility, domicile rules and bond conditions.

sections.heading: Location and campus
paragraphs: Both colleges are in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on different campuses.
Visit the teaching hospital or clinic attached to each college, because clinical training is a large part of a BDS degree.

sections.heading: Verdict: who should pick which college
paragraphs: On this page, only The Oxford Dental College has a recorded year fee, at ₹2.40 lakh. That is not enough, by itself, to name a winner.
Get both official fee circulars and official internship reports before you decide.
Do not invent a fee or a package that we do not hold.
